ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left of the figure is a cyclohexanone fragment, with a carbonyl O connected above the six-membered carbon ring; the upper right of the ring is connected to a nitrogen-containing diazo/aza fragment, and on the right there is also an N–SO2Me sulfonyl methyl group. The central carbon is connected to the ring, nitrogen, and oxygen, and one H is drawn; the figure also has curved arrows and negative charge labels, but the problem requires ignoring arrows and excluding bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning count: Count according to the specified method. The left cyclohexanone fragment has 6 C–C bonds in the six-membered ring, plus 1 C=O bond, 7 in total. The visible bonds in the exocyclic heteroatom/central skeleton are: ring carbon–N, N=N, N–N (the nitrogen connected to the sulfonamide N), N–central C, central C–ring carbon, central C–O, 6 in total. The sulfonyl methyl part is counted as: N–S, two S=O bonds, S–Me carbon bond, 4 in total. Exclude the explicit C–H bond on the central carbon and all implicit hydrogen bonds. Therefore the total number is 7 + 6 + 4 = 17.

method.method_draft: First count the left cyclohexanone fragment: six C–C bonds in the ring plus one C=O bond = 7. Then count the heteroatom/central framework links visible outside the ring: ring carbon–N, N=N, N–N(sulfonyl), N–central C, central C–ring carbon, and central C–O = 6 more. Then count the sulfonyl methyl group: N–S, two S=O bonds, and S–Me carbon = 4 more. Exclude the explicit C–H bond at the central carbon and all implicit hydrogens. Sum 7 + 6 + 4 = 17.
